name: UC3525ADWTR
title: Regulating pulse-width modulators, UCx525A and UCx527A
summary: A family of voltage-mode PWM controllers for switching power supplies, running from 8 V to 35 V. Each has a 5.1 V reference trimmed to 1 %, an error amplifier, an oscillator from 100 Hz to 500 kHz with a sync input and a resistor-set dead time, soft start, a shutdown pin for pulse-by-pulse limiting, undervoltage lockout with hysteresis, a latch against double pulsing and two alternating totem-pole drivers rated 500 mA. The x525A parts hold off outputs low, the x527A parts hold them high; UC1, UC2 and UC3 set the temperature range. UC3525ADWTR is the UC3525A in a 16-pin SOIC on tape and reel.
key_figures: 500 mA source or sink, absolute maximum

notes: UC1525A and UC2525A/UC3525A have NOR output logic: an output that is off sits low. UC1527A, UC2527A and UC3527A have OR logic: an off output sits high.
The first digit sets the temperature grade: UC152xA for -55 °C to 125 °C ambient, UC252xA for -25 °C to 85 °C, UC352xA for 0 °C to 70 °C.
Military (QML) versions: UC1525A, UC1527A, UC2525AM. Catalog versions: UC3525A, UC3527A, UC2525A, UC3525AM.

circuits.title: Lab test fixture
circuits.description: Bench fixture for measuring the controller. Every supply, output and timing node comes out to a jack or test point, and VIN, VC, VREF and the compensation node each carry a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground. RT is 3.6 kΩ and CT is 1 nF, with a jumper that adds 9 nF or 0.1 µF. A 100 Ω dead-time resistor joins Discharge to CT and a switch can short it. The soft-start pin has 5 µF. Shutdown is held at VREF through 5 kΩ and a push button takes it to ground. A 3 kΩ, 10 kΩ pot, 1.5 kΩ chain across VREF gives an adjustable level (PWM Adj.) for the error amplifier. A four-pole, three-position selector puts a voltmeter or ammeter across the amplifier inputs: position 1 reads offset voltage with the amplifier closed through 10 kΩ from Compensation to the inverting input, position 2 puts the meter in series with the non-inverting input, position 3 in series with the inverting input. Each output has a 1 kΩ 1 W load that a ganged switch returns to VC, to ground, or to the output itself (no load).

parts.note: meter selector, meter minus pole; 1 = VOS, 2 = I(+), 3 = I(-)
output A load return, ganged with S6
output B load return, ganged with S5

notes: Switch contacts: S1 to S4 positions 1, 2, 3 are VOS, I(+), I(-). S5 positions 1, 2, 3 return the output A load to output A, VC, ground; S6 positions 1, 2, 3 return the output B load to VC, ground, output B.

circuits.title: Low power transformers
circuits.description: The two outputs drive a gate transformer directly: output A through a series capacitor to one end of the primary, output B to the other end. A Schottky diode from ground to each output clamps it. Each secondary drives one MOSFET of a half bridge through a gate resistor, with a resistor from gate to source. The bridge midpoint drives the power transformer T2, whose other end sits between C1 and C2 across the supply. VC is fed from the supply through a resistor. The core resets in the dead time, while both outputs sit low.

parts.note: gate transformer: primary P1-P2, secondaries S1A-S1B and S2A-S2B

notes: Only the output-stage pins of U1 take part in this circuit.

circuits.title: Grounded driver outputs for single-ended supplies
circuits.description: Both driver outputs are tied to ground and VC becomes the drive: on alternate oscillator cycles the source transistors of the totem poles pull VC to ground. VC connects through R2 to the base of a PNP switch Q1, R1 joins that base to the supply, and Q1's collector feeds the output filter.
notes: Only the output-stage pins of U1 take part in this circuit.

circuits.title: Output drivers with low source impedance
circuits.description: Push-pull MOSFET stage from a 15 V supply. Each output drives a power MOSFET gate through 30 Ω, and the low output impedance charges the gate capacitance quickly with few parts. A UC3611 Schottky diode from ground to each output keeps the pin from ringing below ground. The MOSFET drains go to the ends of the centre-tapped primary of T1, whose centre tap and VC both sit on the 15 V rail.

parts.note: centre-tapped primary: ends P1, P2, tap CT

notes: Misprint: Q2's source returns to ground, as Q1's does.
Only the output-stage pins of U1 take part in this circuit.

circuits.description: Push-pull stage with two NPN power transistors on a centre-tapped transformer. R1 from the supply to VC and the base resistors R2 and R3 set the forward base drive; C1 and C2 across the base resistors speed up turn-off.

operation.text: A voltage-mode PWM controller with a 5.1 V reference trimmed to 1 %, an error amplifier whose common-mode range takes in the reference voltage (so no divider is needed to bias it), an oscillator with a sync input and a programmable dead time, internal soft start, a shutdown input, undervoltage lockout, a latch after the PWM comparator and two totem-pole drivers that switch on alternate cycles. It suits off-line and DC/DC supplies, single-ended or two-switch designs, solar and welding inverters, motor control and battery chargers.

RT and CT set the frequency, 100 Hz to 500 kHz. The sync pin lets several controllers run as slaves of one, or locks one controller to an outside clock. The dead time is set over a wide range by one resistor joining Discharge to CT.
A capacitor from the soft-start pin to ground, charged by the internal 50 µA source, sets the soft-start ramp.
Below the lockout threshold the outputs stay off and the soft-start capacitor is held discharged. The lockout has about 500 mV of hysteresis so it does not chatter.

A latch follows the PWM comparator. Once a pulse ends, for whatever reason, both outputs stay off for the rest of that period; each clock pulse resets the latch, so one period gives at most one pulse.
Each output is a totem pole that sources or sinks more than 200 mA. The UC1525A family uses NOR logic and holds an off output low; the UC1527A family uses OR logic and holds an off output high.

Compensation and soft start both have current-source pull-ups, so pulling either down with a sink of at most 100 µA turns the outputs off, plus whatever current discharges capacitance on that pin. A high level on the Shutdown pin sets the PWM latch at once, the fastest way to end a pulse, and starts a 150 µA sink discharging the soft-start capacitor. A short shutdown pulse ends the PWM pulse without draining much of the soft-start charge, which makes pulse-by-pulse current limiting possible; a long one discharges the capacitor, and the supply restarts slowly when it is released. A floating Shutdown pin can pick up noise that upsets operation, so it is always driven. A change of level on it completes inside one clock cycle, and changes come no more often than once per 10 clock cycles.

The outputs can drive a low-power transformer directly; its core resets in the dead time, while the two outputs hold both primary terminals at ground. For a single-ended supply both outputs are grounded and the source transistors pull VC to ground on alternate cycles. The low output impedance charges power MOSFET gate capacitance quickly. In a bipolar push-pull design, resistors set the base drive and capacitors across the base resistors speed turn-off.

A push-pull converter from 25 V to 35 V (30 V nominal) to 5 V at up to 10 A. The oscillator runs at 100 kHz (RT = 10 kΩ, CT = 1.37 nF, RD = 100 Ω), so each switch runs at 50 kHz; higher frequency means smaller magnetics and more switching loss. With DLIM = 0.35 the turns ratio comes out at 3. Inductor ripple of 20 % to 40 % of full load balances core and copper loss; 25 % of 10 A gives 11.57 µH. The output rectifiers need low forward drop and short recovery time, and Schottky diodes are the recommended choice. The output capacitors filter the ripple from the inductor and carry load transients. The input capacitors keep ripple at the VIN pin down and carry the bulk of the current the switches draw while on; choose them by RMS current rating and ripple.

The VC capacitor supplies the drivers' peak currents, which can reach several amperes, and keeps the VC supply stable. Use at least 0.1 µF, a low-ESR ceramic of good quality, as close to the VC pin as possible so trace inductance cannot cause harmful voltage spikes.
VIN runs from 8 V to 35 V. VC runs from 4.5 V to 35 V, chosen to suit the switching device: 12 V suits a MOSFET, for example.

Lay the circuit over a ground plane. Damp or clamp the inductive kick coming back from a driven MOSFET gate, and keep the outputs from ringing below ground, with a series gate resistor or a 1 A Schottky diode from the output pin to ground. Decouple VIN, VC and VREF each with a 0.1 µF low-ESL monolithic ceramic, keeping the combined lead length between pin and ground plane under 1 cm. Lay out the timing capacitor CT as you would a decoupling capacitor.
ESD protection on chip is limited. Store and handle the parts with the leads shorted together or in conductive foam to protect the MOS gates.
